stories.headline: Juniper Ridge starts its title defense with an open spot at No. 1 singles
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Juniper Ridge won everything there was to win last fall. The Navrang school went 18-0 in the Kajaani League, finished 31-5 and came home from the state tournament with the 5A championship.

What it does not have this year is Rafael Rivera. The No. 1 singles player went 24-6 at the top of the lineup and graduated in June, and nobody on this year's roster spent much of last season at No. 1 singles.

Most of the rest of the group is back, and most of it is old. Seniors Ezekiel Amoore (28-8) and Deon Rennick (28-7) and junior Joshua Butcher (28-5) played the bulk of their matches in doubles, and sophomore Levi Chesnut went 16-0 as a freshman, mostly at No. 2 and No. 3 singles.

"Everybody keeps asking me who plays one," coach Ray Okafor said Saturday after the last practice before the opener. "I'll know after a couple of weeks. Right now I've got four guys who think it's them, and that's the right problem to have."

Juniper Ridge opens Monday at Liberty Hill, a 6A Octofinalist last season, then plays at home Tuesday against Pacersburg and Wednesday against Westfield Friends of Fort Meriwether, a 4A team that went 27-2 a year ago. The Kajaani League schedule starts Thursday at Cedar Exchange.

stories.headline: Carroway brings back its seniors but not its singles players
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Carroway reached the 3A state final last fall and lost it. The Juniper League champions finished 23-4, 14-2 in league play, and then graduated both players who took turns at No. 1 singles, Asher Barrett and Bronson Koontz.
Senior Luke Palm went 23-4, the best record on the team, mostly in doubles. Senior Michael Stevens (20-7) and juniors Primitivo Delgado (18-9) and James Stacy (20-5) are also back.
"We were one match from a title, and the first thing the kids asked me in June was when the lineup sheet goes up," coach Linda Haverkamp said. "It goes up after the first week. Not before."
Carroway opens Wednesday at home against Pacersburg and plays Ostrander Union, last season's league runner-up, in the Juniper League opener on Aug. 8.

stories.headline: County by county: what to watch in Rimrock and Juniper
body: RIMROCK COUNTY

Covenant (7A, Premier Athletic Association): Won the league at 11-1 and finished 20-6, then lost No. 1 singles Brody Dufault to graduation. Seniors Francis Gafford, Daniel Hunter and Travis Weber all played doubles last season and all three are back.
Navrang (6A, Northwest Assembly): A state quarterfinalist at 18-7. Yusuf Aranda, the No. 1, graduated. Seniors Dillon Lemons (20-5) and Dani Snow (17-8) and junior Nehemiah Patel (20-5) return.

Central West End (5A, Kajaani League): Fourth in the league Juniper Ridge won, then an Octofinalist at 21-10. The lineup is almost all seniors. Andrew Brown, Derrick Amrhein, Isaiah Conway and Julian Hall each won 19 or more last season, and Nico Buchner is back after splitting time at No. 1 singles.

Silton Ridge and Vesper (1A, Desert Sky League): The league's top two last season at 14-2 and 12-4, and both reached the state quarterfinals. Silton Ridge graduated its two singles regulars, Michael Carrillo and Cody Klaassen. Vesper sophomore Taras Piątek went 26-3 as a freshman, mostly at No. 1 doubles.

Dry Lake (6A, Fiesta Athletic Association): Second in the league at 10-4 and 19-12 overall, and all four of its busiest players are back: juniors Lawrence Sullivan and Lorenzo Morlan and sophomores Noah Sorenson and Teagan Combs.
JUNIPER COUNTY
California Canyons (3A, Dual County League): League champions at 16-2 and 23-8. Junior Hudson Chiu, 16-12 at No. 1 singles last season, is back at the top of the lineup.
Altamonte (8A, Big Basin League): Eight seniors on the roster. Grant Labbé played No. 1 singles last season and went 8-23. Roman Dukes (20-11) and Anthony Ryu (18-13) carried the doubles.
Senator Gray (8A, Del Rey Athletic Association): Seniors Cranston Diggins (18-10) and John Jensen (20-8) shared the top singles spot last season and both return.
Mt Jacqueline (2A, Three Rivers League): The league runner-up at 12-2 lost both of its No. 1 singles players, Tyler Greene and Max Morisaki. Junior Ryder Nale went 26-4, mostly in doubles.
High Desert Christian (3A, Juniper League): Went 0-16 in the league and 3-24 overall. Its four busiest players last season are seniors now.

stories.headline: Twelve area duals open the season Monday
body: The season opens Monday with 12 invitational duals involving area teams. Juniper Ridge plays at Liberty Hill, and Altamonte and Senator Gray, two of the three 8A schools in the city of Altamonte, meet at Senator Gray.
Silton Ridge travels to Espoo, a 1A state semifinalist last season. Central West End is at Calder, California Canyons at Summervale and Trout Lake at Star Hollow.
